The loop 'for (int tile = blockRow; tile <= blockCol; tile++)' uses blockRow and blockCol directly. ROW_TILES appears exactly once — at its definition — and is never read. Grid dimensions are computed in host code as (N + TILE_SIZE - 1) / TILE_SIZE, independent of the kernel's ROW_TILES variable.

However, ROW_TILES is a dead variable — it is computed but never used anywhere in the kernel code. Since ROW_TILES has no consumers, any change to its value has zero effect on memory accesses, control flow, or output values. This is a classic dead code mutation that is semantically equivalent to the original.

rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should include dead code detection as a pre-filter to avoid generating equivalent mutants from unused variables. Static analysis to identify variables that are written but never read would eliminate this class of unkillable mutants before expensive dynamic testing.
